# SROTrac — full text for AI agents
Source: https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in (CC BY 4.0). One section per page.


## home — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/
Register of India’s financial-sector self-regulatory organisations · RBI · SEBI · IRDAI · IBBI 
 Who watches India’s fintech watchdogs ? 

 Recognised SROs × 18 
 2 × SRO-FT 

 India’s regulators outsource first-line supervision to self-regulatory organisations — industry bodies empowered to write conduct codes and police their own members. SROTrac tracks who sits on them, what they do, and whether they work for consumers — across RBI, SEBI, IRDAI and IBBI , plus the two industry giants (AMFI, ANMI) that self-regulate without ever being recognised. 

 18 SROs tracked 
 4 regulators 
 774 listed member orgs 
 79 in 2+ SROs 
 2 fintech SRO-FTs 

 The register 
 Sixteen recognised bodies across four regulators, plus two unrecognised associations tracked for context. Click a folder for members, governance and activity.

 What is an SRO, in plain words? 
 RBI can't directly supervise thousands of fintechs, NBFCs and payment companies. So it recognises industry associations as self-regulatory organisations — with a contract: broad membership, independent boards, codes of conduct, monitoring of member compliance, and grievance redress. In return the regulator gets a first line of supervision, and the industry gets a single voice. 
 For consumers, the SRO is one more place to escalate when a lender or payment company misbehaves — but only if the SRO actually enforces. That is what this tracker watches: rosters, governance, consultations, enforcement, and the gaps in between.

 People in 2+ SROs 
 Person Roles Jiji Mammen FIDC: Advisory Council; Sa-Dhan: Executive Director & CEO N S Vishwanathan FIDC: Governing Council Member (Additional Director wef 2026-06-23); UFF: Independent Board Member Shachindra Nath FIDC: Governing Council Member; UFF: EC Member Sugandh Saxena FACE: CEO (first CEO; MFIN: Member Secretary 

 Why this matters: the omnibus SRO framework requires SROs to avoid conflicts of interest. Shared directors and EC members across SROs are legal — but when the same fintech executives shape conduct rules at multiple bodies, consumers should know whose interests get harmonised first.


## timeline — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/timeline.html
Regulatory timeline 
 How RBI built the SRO system — frameworks, recognitions, and what each SRO did about it. 

 2026 

 2026-09-10 UFF recognition 
 UFF recognised as India's second SRO-FT 
 RBI granted SRO-FT registration to Unified Fintech Forum (ex-DLAI) ahead of RBI's Global Fintech Fest address; second fintech SRO after FACE. 

 2026-09-01 FIMMDA governance 
 FIMMDA constitutes a Disciplinary Committee of the Board 
 First visible post-recognition enforcement machinery: Disciplinary Committee constituted under Article 34 of its AoA (FIMCIR/2026-27/20) — chaired by Manoj Rane (Independent Director), with Abhijit Basak (Union Bank) and Manish Luharuka (ICICI Bank). 

 2026-08 FACE report 
 FACE Personal Loan Report 2026 
 Consumer-facing study of India's personal loan market: borrower profiles, pricing, top lenders, delinquency and origination trends. 

 2026-06-05 FIDC consultation 
 FIDC views on RBI monetary policy statement (June 2026) 
 FIDC publicly responded to the June 2026 monetary policy, representing NBFC sector interests on liquidity and rate transmission. 

 2026-01-14 FEDAI recognition 
 FEDAI recognised as SRO for all Authorised Dealers 
 RBI recognised FEDAI (est. 1958) as SRO for the foreign-exchange market under the Omnibus SRO framework, with a one-year transition (to Jan 2027) to align governance and extend membership to all AD categories. 

 2025 

 2025-11-11 SRPA recognition 
 SRPA becomes RBI-recognised SRO for payment system operators 
 Self-Regulated PSO Association (SRPA) recognised under the SRO-PSO framework; founded by Vishwas Patel (CCAvenue) and M N Srinivasu (BillDesk); 18 members. 

 2025-10-03 FIDC recognition 
 FIDC recognised as RBI's SRO for NBFCs 
 Finance Industry Development Council became the recognised self-regulatory organisation for NBFCs under the omnibus framework. 

 2025-08 FACE tool 
 DLA Validator — consumer tool for checking digital lending apps 
 FACE's consumer corner offers a DLA (digital lending application) validator so borrowers can check an app before taking a loan. 

 2025-05-08 FIMMDA roster 
 FIMMDA publishes List of Current Members (116 institutions) 
 Member list PDF dated 8 May 2025: 12 public sector banks, 21 private banks, 34 foreign banks, 7 primary dealers, 5 financial institutions, 20 insurers, 11 SFBs, 3 payments banks, CCIL and 2 infrastructure financiers. Only public roster FIMMDA publishes — a PDF, not a web directory. 

 2025-05-07 FIMMDA recognition 
 FIMMDA recognised as RBI's first SRO in financial markets 
 RBI recognised the Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India (est. 1998) as an SRO in the financial markets it regulates (Press Release 2025-2026/274) — the first recognition under the August 2024 financial-markets SRO framework. 

 2025-04-16 UFF announcement 
 DLAI rebrands as Unified Fintech Forum (UFF); new leadership elected 
 DLAI became UFF with ~120 members: Manish Lunia (FlexiLoans) as President, Upasana Taku (MobiKwik) as Vice-President. Sought RBI SRO-FT recognition as a broad fintech body. 

 2025-04 UFF announcement 
 UFF executive committee and working-group chairs in place 
 UFF EC formed: Manish Lunia (President), Upasana Taku (VP & Events Chair), chairs for SRO, Knowledge, Policy/Product/Tech, Events, PR portfolios. 

 2024 

 2024-09 UFF announcement 
 DLAI among fintech bodies that applied to RBI for SRO-FT status 
 Three associations applied for SRO-FT recognition after the final framework; Digital Lenders Association of India's application was returned/kept pending. 

 2024-08-28 FACE recognition 
 FACE becomes India's first RBI-recognised fintech SRO (SRO-FT) 
 Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment recognised as the first SRO-FT, effective from date of issue of certificate of registration. 

 2024-08-14 FACE consultation 
 FACE response to TRAI consultation on DLT-based transaction scrubbing 
 FACE filed detailed views (218 pages, 8 annexures) on TRAI's draft 'The Telecommunications (DLT-based Scrubbing) Regulations, 2025', from the digital-lending industry perspective. 

 2024-06-19 RBI announcement 
 RBI invites applications for recognition of SROs for NBFCs 
 RBI press release inviting SRO applications under the omnibus framework from NBFC industry associations. 

 2024-05-30 RBI framework 
 Final framework for recognising Self-Regulatory Organisations in the fintech sector (SRO-FT) 
 Final SRO-FT framework: recognised SRO-FTs to monitor fintech compliance with regulations and codes, support innovation, and protect consumers. 

 2024-05-16 BASL framework 
 SEBI framework for administration and supervision of research analysts and investment advisers - BSE/BASL designated both IAASB and RAASB 
 Effective 25 Jul 2024: existing IAs who are BASL members and all registered RAs deemed enlisted with the supervisory bodies. 

 2024-03-21 RBI framework 
 Omnibus framework for recognising self-regulatory organisations in regulated financial entities 
 Generic framework applicable across RBI-regulated sectors (NBFCs, PSOs, etc.), each sector supervisor to invite/recognise SROs. 

 2024-01-15 RBI framework 
 Draft framework for recognising Self-Regulatory Organisations for the fintech sector (SRO-FT) 
 RBI's first fintech-specific SRO framework: eligibility, membership openness, governance, oversight of members' compliance and consumer protection. 

 2023 

 2023-09 FACE partnership 
 Google x FACE collaboration against predatory digital lending apps 
 Partnership to identify and act against predatory lending apps on Android; part of FACE's consumer-protection and app-fraud agenda. 

 2021 

 2021-08 FACE announcement 
 FACE applies to RBI for SRO recognition (digital lending) 
 FACE was among the first industry bodies to apply to RBI for SRO status in digital lending, months after the draft framework chatter began. 

 2021-06-01 BASL recognition 
 SEBI recognises BASL (BSE Administration and Supervision Ltd) as the Investment Adviser Administration and Supervisory Body (IAASB) 
 Three-year recognition from 1 Jun 2021; all SEBI-registered investment advisers deemed enlisted with BASL. First supervisory body of its kind for IAs. 

 2020 

 2020-10-22 RBI framework 
 Framework for recognition of Self-Regulatory Organisation for Payment System Operators (SRO-PSO) 
 First SRO framework in payments: Recognised associations of PSOs to set standards, ensure compliance, and address grievances. Enabled payments SROs under Section 43A/43E PSS Act. 

 2020-10-22 RBI framework 
 Omnibus framework path: PSO + RBI SRO-FT + sector SROs 
 RBI's omnibus framework for recognising SROs across regulated entities set the template later used for NBFC (FIDC), PSO (SRPA) and FX (FEDAI) SRO recognition. 

 2015 

 2015-03-11 RBI recognition 
 Sa-Dhan recognised as SRO for NBFC-MFIs 
 RBI recognition made Sa-Dhan the second microfinance SRO, giving NBFC-MFIs a choice of SRO membership. 

 2014 

 2014-06-16 MFIN recognition 
 MFIN becomes India's first SRO for NBFC-MFIs 
 RBI letter dated 16 June 2014 accorded MFIN recognition as the first self-regulatory organisation of NBFC-MFIs, post-Andhra crisis (Malegam committee route).

Social media monitor · tracked SROs 
 Where the SROs post 
 Codes of conduct, consultation responses and discipline machinery often surface first on an SRO’s own channels — usually LinkedIn, sometimes X. This page tracks every official account of the tracked SROs, and the daily refresh re-checks each one against the SRO’s own website. ✓ = still linked from the SRO’s site today · ✎ = verified via the SRO’s own announcement or platform search.

 How this is monitored 

 The daily refresh re-fetches the SROs’ own pages, then a drift check ( scripts/social_check.py ) confirms every ✓-marked account is still linked from its official site. Last drift check 2026-09-26: 23/23 official-site links still live. 
 X, LinkedIn, Facebook and Instagram block robots, so follower counts and post contents are not scraped here — links are curated, dated (verified 2026-09-25) and re-verified in the direction platforms can’t block: the SRO’s own website. 
 A handle vanishing from an official site is the cheapest early signal of a rebrand, a takeover or a quietly deleted account — it shows here as a ⚠ flag. 
 Spotted a new or dead handle? It’s a one-row fix in data/social.csv (CC BY 4.0).


## about — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/about.html
About SROTrac 
 An independent, open-data register of India's RBI-recognised self-regulatory organisations — built by CashlessConsumer, a consumer collective working on digital payments and fintech. Licensed CC BY 4.0 (data) and MIT (code). 

 Scope: RBI’s SROs only 
 India has several self-regulatory bodies across financial regulators. SROTrac tracks only the nine recognised by the Reserve Bank of India : the two SRO-FTs (FACE, UFF), FIDC (NBFCs), SRPA (payment operators), MFIN and Sa-Dhan (microfinance), FEDAI (authorised dealers), Sahamati (Account Aggregator ecosystem), and FIMMDA (fixed income, money market and derivatives). Bodies under other regulators — e.g. AMFI and IIFL under SEBI, the Insurance Institute under IRDAI — are not covered here, however senior their profiles. 

 Method 

 Member rosters are parsed from each SRO's own published member pages (captured 2026-09-10 ). 
 Governance data comes from SRO governance/leadership pages; roles are quoted as published. 
 The activity log links only to primary sources (RBI press releases, TRAI filings, SRO pages) or dated news reports. 
 The SRPA roster was decoded from its logo wall (filenames are truncated) — treat spelling with care. 
 Everything rebuilds from CSV via a single script; the GitHub repo carries the raw captures. 

 Caveats 

 SRO member pages are marketing pages, not registers . FACE claims 200+ members but shows ~85 logos; treat counts as a floor. 
 FIDC publishes no member roster at all — its "list of NBFCs" page holds RBI registration statistics, not membership. 
 Membership changes constantly; dates matter. Each dataset notes its capture date. 
 Recognition ≠ effectiveness. An SRO can be fully compliant on paper and still never discipline a member. This tracker will log enforcement actions as they surface. 

 FAQ 
 Which SROs does India have? The Reserve Bank of India has recognised nine self-regulatory organisations: FACE and UFF for fintech (SRO-FT framework), FIDC for NBFCs, SRPA for payment system operators, MFIN and Sa-Dhan for microfinance lenders, FEDAI for authorised dealers in foreign exchange, Sahamati for the account aggregator ecosystem, and FIMMDA for the fixed income, money market and derivatives markets. Does SROTrac cover SEBI or IRDAI industry bodies? No. SROTrac tracks only RBI-recognised SROs. Bodies like AMFI (mutual funds) or the Insurance Institute are recognised by other regulators and are out of scope. Is SROTrac affiliated with the RBI or any SRO? No. SROTrac is an independent project by CashlessConsumer, a consumer collective. It uses only publicly available sources: SRO websites, RBI press releases and dated news reports. Is Sahamati recognised by the RBI? Yes. RBI recognised Sahamati as the SRO for the account aggregator (AA) ecosystem on 5 June 2026. Before recognition, Sahamati spent five years as the AA ecosystem's non-profit standards body (spun out of iSPIRT's work). Its directory lists 110 regulated entities across AAs, FIPs, FIUs and TSPs. How many members do the SROs have? As of the latest capture: FACE 85, UFF 121, SRPA 18, MFIN 84, FEDAI 108, Sahamati 110, FIMMDA 116, AMFI 56, GI Council 49 and LI Council 27 listed members — 774 rows across the 18 tracked bodies. FIDC, Sa-Dhan, BASL, AIBI and the three IBBI IPAs publish no public roster. Counts are floors, not filings: SRO member pages are marketing pages. Can I reuse the data? Yes. Data is licensed CC BY 4.0 — copy, remix and republish with attribution to SROTrac / CashlessConsumer. The CSVs are linked on the members page and in the GitHub repo.

## FACE register entry — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/sro-face.html
RBI · SRO register 
 Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment FACE 
 Deep-dive: what FACE actually does → 
 Fintech / digital lending 

 Recognised (RBI) 2024-08-28 
 Status Active SRO-FT 
 Listed members 85 (37 Fintech / LSP · 18 Tech / TSP · 13 Payments / PSO · 10 NBFC) 
 Site faceofindia.org 

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay 
 Runs the DLA Validator — check a lending app before you borrow from it. Publishes a Grievance & Dispute Resolution (GDR) framework and an Oversight & Enforcement policy for members. Studies personal-loan pricing and borrower outcomes (Personal Loan Report 2026) and pushed Google on predatory lending apps. 

 What we're watching 
 Member count claims (~200+) vs published roster (~85 logos) — the public list is a marketing page, not a register. Enforcement actions are not published; the SRO-FT framework expects oversight of member conduct.

## FACE work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-face.html
What FACE actually does 
 Fintech Association for Consumer Empowerment FACE 
 Standards, oversight & dispute resolution for digital lending 

 FACE (registered 24 August 2020, recognised 28 August 2024) is the first RBI-recognised SRO-FT. Its published work splits into five streams: standards, oversight & enforcement, grievance & dispute resolution (GDR), policy engagement, and knowledge tooling. 
 Standards & guidelines (dated trail) Guidelines on Arbitration Framework in Loan Agreement — 2 Sep 2026 Guidelines on DLG (Default Loss Guarantee) disclosure — Jul 2026 Guidelines for LSP–RE agreements (lending service provider ↔ regulated entity) — 31 Mar 2026 Guidelines on Whistleblower Mechanism — Sep 2025 Guidelines on Debt Recovery — 29 Aug 2025 Guidelines on Penal Charges — Jun 2025 Guidelines on Cybersecurity Measures — 13 May 2025 Pricing of Digital Loans by NBFCs — Jan 2025 Practical tooling for members List of Regulatory Policies for base-layer NBFCs — 31 Aug 2026 List of Supervisory Returns for NBFCs — 28 Aug 2026 Checklist for Responsible & Trustworthy AI in digital lending (with Dvara and PwC) — 18 Mar 2026 Checklist for public disclosure on DLAs and LSP/RE websites — 14 Aug 2025 Checklist on Customer Grievance Redressal — 13 Mar 2024; defence guide against unauthorised use of company details — 4 Mar 2024 Baseline technology standards suggestions for DLAs — Mar 2023 Oversight & enforcement The Oversight & Enforcement Policy (18 Aug 2025) sets out monitoring, review, escalation and enforcement across self-regulatory work: company-level monitoring, industry-level pattern analysis (including tracking app marketplaces), distinguishing isolated lapses from recurring deviations, with escalation paths to member-support, cautions, and RBI referral. Grievance & dispute resolution (GDR) A governed pathway for member disputes and complaints: submission via prescribed digital channels → initial review by the nodal officer and CEO → escalation to the Grievance and Dispute Redressal Committee → examination → formal closure. Documented, confidential, time-bound; positioned as an alternative to escalation and litigation. Policy & knowledge work Consultation responses and structured dialogue with RBI, government and regulators — engagement framed as evidence-based and balanced across buy/sell side Industry surveys and reports under its Knowledge stream; member-only advisories Client-insight channel and engagement with marketplaces and app ecosystems 
 Gaps & open questions The DAK (Digital Assurance & Keeping?) scorecard detail referenced in its framework pages is not published as a standalone document No public complaint statistics or enforcement actions register Full member agreements/code sign-offs are not public 
 Sources faceofindia.org — Standards FACE — Oversight & Enforcement Policy FACE — Grievance & Dispute Resolution FACE — Policy FACE — Governance 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from FACE’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry


## UFF register entry — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/sro-uff.html
RBI · SRO register 
 Unified Fintech Forum UFF 
 Deep-dive: what UFF actually does → 
 Fintech (broad): lenders, wallets/PPIs, neobanks, BNPL 

 Recognised (RBI) 2026-09-10 
 Status Active SRO-FT (recognised at GFF 2026) 
 Listed members 121 (39 Fintech / LSP · 32 NBFC · 21 Tech / TSP · 13 Other / Services) 
 Site unifiedfintech.in 

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay 
 Second RBI-recognised fintech SRO — now both major fintech lobbies are under RBI's SRO-FT rules: codes of conduct, member monitoring, grievance redress. Has a dedicated SRO portfolio in its Executive Committee (Chair: Progcap; Co-chair: Vivifi) — the desk expected to police members. Independent board stacked with ex-regulators: two former RBI Deputy Governor/ED-level officials, ex-CMD of SIDBI, ex-SBI Deputy MD. 

 What we're watching 
 Freshly recognised — codes of conduct and enforcement machinery are yet to be tested in public. Track whether UFF publishes member-discipline actions, unlike FACE's unpublished enforcement record.

## UFF work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-uff.html
What UFF actually does 
 Unified Fintech Forum UFF 
 Digital lending's second SRO-FT: born as DLAI, recognised 10 Sep 2026 

 The Unified Fintech Forum (formerly the Digital Lenders Association of India, founded 2016) became RBI's second fintech SRO on 10 September 2026. Its self-described remit spans the fintech stack — digital lending, payments, wealthtech, insurtech — with working groups under a governance council and a secretariat. 
 Governance architecture Independent-dominated board: Alok Prasad (Chair) with ex-RBI Deputy Governor N S Vishwanathan, ex-RBI ED Meena Hemchandra, ex-SBI Deputy MD Dhananjay Tambe, ex-SIDBI CMD Mohammad Mustafa and others alongside founder-member promoters (Indifi, Freo, Axio, Lendingkart) Governance Council, committees, working groups, and a Code-of-Conduct sub-committee under its published governance philosophy Professional secretariat; executive committee drawn from member CEOs Client protection work Voluntary Code of Conduct for digital lenders — developed pre-SRO as a market benchmark that fed into the RBI's digital lending framework Capacity building and collaborations on predatory lending, harassment and fraud concerns Public trust positioning: consumer research and fair-recovery / collections norms advocacy Policy & consultation engagement Position papers and consultation responses to RBI, Ministry of Finance, MeitY and NITI Aayog Roundtables with policymakers; the association advocated for the SRO-FT framework it now operates under Publications: whitepapers and industry reports via its publications portal 
 Gaps & open questions The UFF Code of Conduct text is not published as a downloadable PDF on its site No published member disciplinary/enforcement log yet (SRO licence granted 10 Sep 2026 — early days) Member counts claimed in press (~200+) vs the site's own member wall (121 listed) — treat roster as directional 
 Sources UFF — Governance & Secretariat UFF — Client Protection UFF — Policy & Advocacy UFF — Publications 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from UFF’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay

 What we're watching

## FIDC work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-fidc.html
What FIDC actually does 
 Finance Industry Development Council FIDC 
 NBFCs' SRO: the most active consultation respondent 

 FIDC (Section 8 company, incorporated 10 August 2011; recognised 3 October 2025) is the SRO for NBFCs — a broader, older sector than fintech lending. Its distinctive published work is a dense, dated trail of policy representations and member advisories, plus a governing council of 14 drawn from the biggest NBFC groups. 
 Policy representations (selected, dated) Feedback on RBI draft circular on Interest Rate on Loans — 11 Sep 2026 Revolving credit feedback — 27 Aug 2026; credit-risk implications of AGR — 11 Aug 2026 Responsible Business Conduct comments — 30 May 2026; eNACH feedback — 25 May 2026 Comments on prevention of financial fraud via voice/SMS — 24 Dec 2025 Regulatory parity for loan-against-shares (LAS) — 8 Dec 2025; pre-budget memorandum FY2026-27 Feedback on scale-based regulation amendments — 21 Nov 2025; lending to related parties — 20 Oct 2025 Member advisories (selected) GST on co-lending arrangements — 13 Mar 2025 Fair Business Practices advisory — 23 Dec 2024 Code of Conduct — 11 Jan 2024; Vision Document for NBFCs — 11 Jan 2024 Outsourcing guidelines — 14 Oct 2022; microfinance code of conduct — 4 Oct 2022 COVID-19 moratorium advisory — 4 Apr 2020 Governance & advocacy machinery Governing Council of 14: Chair Umesh Revankar (EVC, Shriram Finance), Vice-Chair Sanjay Gulati (Aditya Birla Finance), with representatives of Tata Sons, Bajaj Finance, Cholamandalam, L&T Finance, Piramal and others CEO Raman Agrawal; committee structure covering regulations, taxation and state-level advocacy Members asked to follow RBI's Fair Practices Code; FIDC positions itself as the NBFC sector's single voice 
 Gaps & open questions No public member roster — annual reports 2019-20 through 2025-26 contain no member list; the only register found is the 14-name Section-8 register in the 15th Annual Report (2018-19) Claims 400+ members in PR materials — unverifiable from its own publications Advisories are PDF-backed but many sit behind vague page links; some circulars are member-only 
 Sources FIDC — Representation FIDC — Advisories FIDC — 22nd Annual Report 2025-26 (PDF) FIDC — 15th Annual Report 2018-19 (member register)

## SRPA work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-srpa.html
What SRPA actually does 
 Self-Regulated PSO Association SRPA 
 Payment aggregators' young SRO: founded by practitioners, one year old 

 SRPA (recognised 11 November 2025) is the youngest SRO — founded by payment-system operators, with CCAvenue's Vishwas Patel and BillDesk's M N Srinivasu on its board. Its first-year output is deliberately narrow: a code of conduct, market-integrity cautions, and DPIIT recognition plumbing. 
 Code of conduct & standards Code of Conduct adopted 8 Jan 2026 — fair merchant pricing, transparent onboarding, consumer data protection EMI and chargeback standards in draft per its public materials Marketplace-integrity positioning against onboarding fraud Ecosystem & trust work Caution circulars aligned with RBI and police cyber-CID warnings on payment fraud DPIIT recognition application (industry status for PA sector) Merchant-education advocacy; 18 payment operators on its partner wall (Razorpay, PhonePe, CRED, MobiKwik, Mswipe, SabPaisa, PayU and others) 
 Gaps & open questions Site is sparse — no roster page with membership categories or join dates; logos are the only roster signal No published enforcement or complaint-handling framework yet Founding date/entity registration details not published on the site 
 Sources SRPA — home (partner wall, code of conduct) 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from SRPA’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry


## MFIN register entry — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/sro-mfin.html
RBI · SRO register 
 Microfinance Institutions Network MFIN 
 Deep-dive: what MFIN actually does → 
 NBFC-MFIs (+ banks/SFBs lending microfinance as associate members) 

 Recognised (RBI) 2014-06-16 
 Status Active SRO (microfinance; RBI letter 16 Jun 2014 — first SRO in this family) 
 Listed members 84 (34 NBFC · 31 NBFC-MFI · 9 Small Finance Bank · 8 Bank) 
 Site mfinindia.org 

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay 
 India's oldest RBI-recognised SRO in this set — created after the 2010 Andhra Pradesh microfinance crisis on the Malegam committee's recommendation. Runs a code of conduct with field-level monitoring and its own dispute-resolution machinery for micro-borrower complaints. 84 member institutions listed on its member wall, from Fusion, Asirvad and CreditAccess Grameen to bank lenders like Axis, HDFC and ICICI. 

 What we're watching 
 Roster is a logo wall organised by region — no join/exit dates published. Site text says 53 primary members (Mar 2025) but the logo wall shows 84 organisations — the extra tiles are likely associates; MFIN does not label them. Microfinance distress and RBI tightening make MFIN's enforcement record the one to watch for borrower-side harm. 

 Governance

## MFIN work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-mfin.html
What MFIN actually does 
 Microfinance Institutions Network MFIN 
 The original SRO experiment: NBFC-MFIs since 16 June 2014 

 MFIN (formed Sep 2013; RBI recognition letter dated 16 June 2014) was the first sector SRO under RBI's 2011 NBFC-MFI direction. Its SRO machinery — supervision, field visits, watchlists, client protection — is a decade old and is the template the fintech SRO-FTs are now judged against. 
 SRO functions & supervision Monitoring member compliance with RBI's NBFC-MFI direction and the industry Code of Conduct Field assessment visits and a Self-Assessment & Monitoring Tool for members Interest-rate monitoring and public rates disclosure for NBFC-MFIs Early-warning watchlists; institutional-level risk analysis Client protection & consumer touchpoints Toll-free customer helpline 1800-102-1080 and customercomplaint@mfinindia.org for grievances against member NBFC-MFIs Client-protection code framework aligned to global SMART-Campaign practice Collector training and conduct standards for field recovery agents Data & industry reporting Quarterly industry data capture (Microscope) covering the large majority of NBFC-MFI loan volumes Annual state-of-sector reporting; district-level outreach studies Membership structure 53 primary NBFC-MFI members; an Associate programme admits banks, SFBs, wholesale/direct NBFCs, credit bureaus, insurers, payment banks, fintechs and telcos — which is why its site wall shows ~84 organisations Governance: board chaired by Devesh Sachdev (Fusion Microfinance founder) with former RBI ED Arnab Roy as independent member; CEO Dr Alok Misra 
 Gaps & open questions Primary-member roster (the 53) is not published as a clean list; the public wall mixes members and associates Enforcement actions and watchlist contents are not public 
 Sources MFIN — SRO recognition (16 Jun 2014) MFIN — Client protection & associates MFIN — Leadership

## Sa-Dhan work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-sadhan.html
What Sa-Dhan actually does 
 Sa-Dhan (Association of Community Development Finance Institutions) Sa-Dhan 
 Community-development finance's SRO: standards since 2015 

 Sa-Dhan (RBI recognition 2015) is the SRO for the microfinance and community-development finance sector. Its published SRO practice is the most tool-like of the older SROs: field assessment, self-assessment instruments, district-level studies and an annual statistical benchmark (Bharat Microfinance Report). 
 SRO tools & supervision Regular Field Assessment Visits to member MFIs Self-Assessment & Monitoring Tool; institutional-level risk analysis Credit Assessment Framework; district-level microfinance status studies Compliance Officer mechanism anchoring SRO processes Consumer touchpoints GRM toll-free grievance number 1800-8899-270 Industry Code of Conduct; Sankalp guardrails for sector conduct District-wise interest-rate tracking and publication Data & benchmarking Bharat Microfinance Report — the sector's annual statistical benchmark Quarterly microfinance reports; '10 Years As SRO' retrospective (2015-2025) 
 Gaps & open questions Member roster not published (claims 200+ institutions in PR materials) GRM outcomes/complaint statistics not published

## FEDAI work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-fedai.html
What FEDAI actually does 
 Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India FEDAI 
 Authorised dealers' rulebook: 30 years of forex standards 

 FEDAI (established 12 Feb 1995; recognised as AD SRO 14 January 2026) has long set the rules for forex business among banks — quoting practices, risk management, broker accreditation — and runs the sector's training machinery. Recognition formalised its role in RBI's new AD-SRO framework. 
 Rule-making & standards Frames rules for forex business inter se ADs (with RBI approval): quotation, documentation, risk practices Accreditation framework for foreign-exchange brokers Daily reference-rate and market-convention publications (incl. USD/INR 10-year LAV) Training & committees Workshop calendar: 5-day orientation programmes, FX-derivative workshops with Bloomberg, TBML counter-measures, LC documentation Technical Advisory Committee (16 banks) and an Education Committee; local committees across centres Managing Committee chaired by State Bank of India, with DBS Bank India as Vice Chairman Membership 108 Authorised Dealer members with LEIs (published list with categories: foreign banks incl. branches, PSBs, private banks, SFBs, others) Liaison role between RBI and ADs on forex-market operations 
 Gaps & open questions Rule books and circular archives require member access; the public site publishes only summaries As an AD SRO recognised in Jan 2026, its SRO-period enforcement record is still building 
 Sources FEDAI — About FEDAI — Managing Committee FEDAI — Member banks FEDAI — Workshops

## Sahamati register entry — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/sro-sahamati.html
RBI · SRO register 
 Sahamati 
 Deep-dive: what Sahamati actually does → 
 Account Aggregator (AA) ecosystem — AAs, FIPs, FIUs, TSPs 

 Recognised (RBI) 2026-06-05 
 Status Active SRO (AA ecosystem; 8th RBI-recognised SRO) 
 Listed members 110 (31 NBFC · 16 Investments / Wealth · 12 Tech / TSP · 12 Bank) 
 Site sahamati.org.in 

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay 
 The 8th RBI-recognised SRO (5 Jun 2026) and the first for open finance — it governs the account aggregator network you may use to share bank statements with a lender or app. 110 ecosystem REs listed: account aggregators, banks/NBFCs as data providers (FIPs), data consumers (FIUs) and tech service providers — searchable in the members table. For customers: Sahamati's dashboards track AA usage and grievances; if a fintech misuses your consented financial data, the AA framework is where accountability begins. 

 What we're watching 
 Young SRO for a consent-based data ecosystem — watch how it handles complaints against FIUs and whether Fair Use rules get teeth. Roster mixes differently-regulated entities (RBI banks, SEBI brokers, IRDAI insurers); cross-regulator discipline is its hardest test. 

 Governance 
 No published governance page.

## Sahamati work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-sahamati.html
What Sahamati actually does 
 Sahamati Sahamati 
 Standards body of the account-aggregator ecosystem — now its RBI-recognised SRO 

 Sahamati (non-profit catalyst for the Account Aggregator rail since 2020; recognised as the AA ecosystem's SRO on 5 June 2026) is the eighth and newest entry in RBI's SRO register. Its 110 RE members span AAs, FIPs, FIUs and TSPs, and it publishes operational dashboards no other SRO matches. 
 What Sahamati is Sahamati began in 2020 as a non-profit ecosystem catalyst for the Account Aggregator (AA) framework — the RBI-regulated consent-based data-sharing rail that lets customers pull their financial data (bank accounts, investments, GST, insurance) into any FIU app with revocable, purpose-bound consent. Spun out of iSPIRT's product-thought work, it coordinated AAs, FIPs, FIUs and TSPs for five years before the RBI’s omnibus SRO framework gave it a formal home: recognised on 5 June 2026 as the SRO for the AA ecosystem. Membership 110 RE members listed in its Current RE Members directory (captured 2026-09-11) — the widest net of any new SRO: the eight licensed AAs plus FIPs (banks, AMCs, depositories), FIUs (lenders, wealth apps) and TSPs. Membership categories mirror AA-ecosystem roles rather than legal form — a design choice worth watching as RBI's SRO rules technically cover 'regulated entities'. Published infrastructure AA Usage Metrics & Industry Stats dashboards — volumes of consents, data requests and fulfilled requests across the network. Grievances Dashboard — complaint volumes and resolution rates, self-published by the industry body itself. AA APIs Health Dashboard and Central Registry status — operational transparency tools no other SRO runs. Certification and FIP-AA integration playbooks — de facto standards for onboarding data providers. What to watch Enforcement record: dashboards show volumes, but no public disciplinary actions yet — the shift from catalyst to regulator is untested. Scope question: TSPs are not RBI-regulated entities; how an SRO recognised under the omnibus framework governs them remains to be seen. Conflict optics: Sahamati both promotes AA adoption and polices it — the dual hat the omnibus rules ask SROs to manage. 
 Gaps & open questions No public disciplinary/enforcement log yet — dashboards show volumes, not actions. Board, EC and conflict-of-interest disclosures are thinner than FACE's published governance. Unclear how TSPs (not RBI-regulated) sit inside an omnibus-framework SRO. 
 Sources Current RE Members Industry stats & dashboards SRO recognition (what-we-do) 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from Sahamati’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry


## FIMMDA register entry — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/sro-fimmda.html
RBI · SRO register 
 Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India FIMMDA 
 Deep-dive: what FIMMDA actually does → 
 Financial markets: fixed income, money market and derivatives (banks, primary dealers, insurers, public financial institutions) 

 Recognised (RBI) 2025-05-07 
 Status Active SRO (financial markets; first under the Aug 2024 framework) 
 Listed members 116 (66 Bank · 19 Insurer · 11 Small Finance Bank · 8 Development FI) 
 Site www.fimmda.org 

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay 
 The bond and money-market rules your mutual fund, pension fund and insurer trade under are drafted here — FIMMDA sets market practices, standard agreements and the code of fair conduct for the fixed-income market. RBI mandates its valuation of government bonds, corporate bonds and securitised papers — the daily prices that sit inside nearly every debt portfolio in the country. Constituted a Disciplinary Committee (1 Sep 2026, chaired by an independent director) — the enforcement machinery its new SRO status requires. 

 What we're watching 
 Its overview page claims a “115 member strong” body (13 PSBs, 19 private banks, 35 foreign banks…) — its own member-list PDF (8 May 2025) shows 116 rows with different category counts, and the list has not been refreshed since. Recognised on 7 May 2025; disciplinary committee only constituted 16 months later (Sep 2026) — enforcement record starts from zero. Website is a legacy frameset and the roster ships as a PDF — public disclosure lags peer SROs like FEDAI.

## FIMMDA work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-fimmda.html
What FIMMDA actually does 
 Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India FIMMDA 
 The bond market's own rulebook: valuations, market practices and standard agreements 

 FIMMDA (incorporated 4 May 1998) is the oldest market body in the register and the first SRO recognised in the financial markets (7 May 2025, RBI PR 2025-2026/274) under RBI's August 2024 financial-markets SRO framework. Its 116 listed members span public, private, foreign, small-finance and payments banks, primary dealers, insurers, development institutions and CCIL. 
 What FIMMDA does Principal interface with RBI, SEBI and the Ministry of Finance for the fixed income, money and derivatives markets RBI-mandated valuation of government bonds, corporate bonds and securitised papers — the daily prices that bank and primary-dealer portfolios are marked at Standardisation of market practices: FIMMDA Operational Circulars, the Handbook of Market Practices, standard legal agreements (MRA, GMRA, CDS) and the Code of Fair Practices Developmental role: introduced benchmarks (MIBOR history), new products (CPs, securitised papers, OIS) and runs an extensive training programme Membership 116 members in its published list (PDF dated 8 May 2025): 12 public-sector banks, 21 private banks, 34 foreign banks, 7 primary dealers, 5 financial institutions (Exim, NABARD, NHB, SIDBI, NaBFID), 20 insurers, 11 SFBs, 3 payments banks, CCIL, IFCI and IIFCL Fee model: Rs 2.5 lakh one-time registration + Rs 2.5 lakh annual membership (+GST) — an institution-funded body Accredited brokers in the interest-rate-derivatives voice market are governed by a separate accreditation framework and code of conduct SRO transition since recognition Site header now brands FIMMDA a 'Self-Regulatory Organisation in the Financial Markets Regulated by RBI' Disciplinary Committee of the Board constituted 1 Sep 2026 (Art. 34 AoA): chaired by independent director Manoj Rane, with nominee directors from Union Bank and ICICI Bank Nine-member Board (Sep 2026) led by Shamsher Singh (SBI DMD, Global Markets) as Chairman and Neeraj Gambhir (Axis) as Vice Chairman, with three independent directors Standing committees cover new products, technical market practices, membership, valuation, accreditation of brokers, CDS and skill development 
 Gaps & open questions Overview page still claims a '115 member strong' body with category counts that do not match its own 116-row PDF — and the list has not been refreshed since 8 May 2025 No public disciplinary actions, consultation responses or member circular archive without login; circulars are one-page PDFs Legacy frameset website: rosters and disclosures ship as PDFs, not structured pages 
 Sources RBI press release — FIMMDA recognised as SRO (7 May 2025) FIMMDA member list (PDF, 8 May 2025) FIMMDA — Board of Directors FIMMDA — Committees FIMCIR/2026-27/20 — Constitution of Disciplinary Committee (1 Sep 2026)

 BSE Administration and Supervision Ltd BASL 
 Deep-dive: what BASL actually does → 
 Investment advisers (IAASB) + research analysts (RAASB) 

 Recognised (SEBI) 2021-06-01 
 Status Active SRO-body (IAASB + RAASB) 
 Listed members n/p (no public roster) 
 Site www.basl.in 

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay 
 Every SEBI-registered investment adviser — anyone paid to advise you on stocks or MFs — is deemed a BASL member; SEBI's 2024 framework made BSE/BASL also the supervisory body (RAASB) for research analysts . Runs registration vetting, compliance supervision and grievance handling for the advice industry; recognised as IAASB for a 3-year term from 1 Jun 2021, continuing under the 2024 supervisory-body framework. If your adviser or a Telegram 'research analyst' rips you off, BASL's complaint desk is the industry-level stop before SEBI. 

 What we're watching 
 No public member roster. Membership derives from SEBI's IA/RA registers, but BASL publishes no list, no inspection outcomes, no action counts. The IAASB recognition began as a 3-year term (Jun 2021) — watch renewal terms and how many advisers actually face action.

## BASL work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-basl.html
What BASL actually does 
 BSE Administration and Supervision Ltd BASL 
 Administration and supervision of investment advisers and research analysts (SEBI) 

 BASL (BSE Administration & Supervision Ltd), a wholly-owned BSE subsidiary, was recognised by SEBI as the Investment Adviser Administration and Supervisory Body (IAASB) for three years from 1 June 2021. Under SEBI's April 2024 framework (circular of 16 May 2024, effective 25 July 2024), BSE/BASL also administers research analysts as the RAASB. Every SEBI-registered IA is deemed a BASL member; every registered RA is deemed enlisted with the RAASB. 
 Mandate & machinery Administration: enrolment/membership of investment advisers, fee collection, record-keeping for the IA and RA pools. Supervision: monitoring compliance with the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations 2013 and RA Regulations 2014, inspections and complaint handling. Half-yearly reporting to SEBI on supervision of the adviser/analyst pools. Membership All SEBI-registered investment advisers are deemed BASL members (no opt-in list is published). Research analysts deemed enlisted with the RAASB from 25 July 2024. 
 Gaps & open questions No public member roster or complaint statistics — membership is defined by SEBI registers, not by a BASL page. Recognition has been extended in multi-year terms; extension decisions are not logged on the BASL site in a dated, easily auditable way. Supervisory output (inspections, warnings, expulsions) has no public, dated trail yet — the key watch item. 
 Sources RIAs have to register with BASL — Morningstar SEBI framework for supervision of RAs and IAs — Moneycontrol BASL website 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from BASL’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry

## AIBI work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-aibi.html
What AIBI actually does 
 Association of Investment Bankers of India AIBI 
 SEBI-recognised standards body for investment (merchant) bankers 

 The Association of Investment Bankers of India (AIBI, formerly the Association of Merchant Bankers of India, AMBI) holds SEBI recognition recorded since the SEBI Annual Report 1997-98 'to set up professional standards... and establish standard practices in investment banking'. It is the investment-banking industry's sole representative body to SEBI, with 109 members on its own count. 
 Mandate & machinery Professional standards and standard practices for merchant/investment banking activity. Representation on SEBI's Primary Market Advisory Committee (via its Chairperson). Annual summits with the SEBI Chairman as chief guest; seminars, panels, research initiatives and an e-magazine; due-diligence guidance material for members. Membership 109 members (aibi.org.in counter, 2026-09-26). Voluntary membership, but a valid SEBI merchant-banking licence is an eligibility requirement. Life membership (Rs 5,00,000 + GST entrance) and associate membership tiers. 
 Gaps & open questions No public member roster — member.asp is a join/download page, and the roster is available only on request. No published enforcement, complaint or disciplinary record — standards exist as guidance, not as an enforced code with a dated trail. 
 Sources About AIBI AIBI website SEBI Annual Report 1997-98 (AMBI recognition) 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from AIBI’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry


## LI Council register entry — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/sro-lic.html
IRDAI · SRO register 
 Life Insurance Council LI Council 
 Deep-dive: what LI Council actually does → 
 Life insurers (entire industry) 

 Recognised (IRDAI) 1938 (s.64C) 
 Status Active statutory SRO (life insurance) 
 Listed members n/p (no public roster) 
 Site http://www.lifeinscouncil.org 

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay 
 The entire life-insurance industry self-regulates here by statute — s.64C of the Insurance Act, 1938, not a regulator's discretionary recognition. Publishes the industry's code of conduct; its own member list covers 27 life insurers, LIC to Acko Life. Beyond the insurance ombudsman, this council is the industry-level body a life-policy grievance escalates through. 

 What we're watching 
 Statutory status from 1938 predates IRDAI (1999) — the council's independence from the insurers that fund it is structural, not chosen. The website publishes little on member discipline; watch for gaps vs IRDAI's own action counts.

## LI Council work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-lic.html
What LI Council actually does 
 Life Insurance Council LI Council 
 Statutory self-regulatory council for life insurance (Insurance Act s.64C, IRDAI) 

 The Life Insurance Council is the statutory self-regulatory body of India's life-insurance industry, constituted under section 64C of the Insurance Act, 1938. Its member roster spans the life industry — from LIC to private insurers and new entrants — and its remit covers efficiency, public interest, advice to government/IRDAI, and education via affiliated insurance institutes. 
 Statutory role Promote efficiency among life insurers, advance the public interest, and advise government and IRDAI on the industry's growth. Runs education and training through affiliated insurance institutes; publishes the industry year book and journals. Membership (captured 2026-09-26) 27 life insurers listed on lifeinscouncil.org — LIC, private insurers (HDFC Life, SBI Life, ICICI Prudential Life...), and recent entrants (Acko Life, CreditAccess Life). Council office-bearers are drawn from member-insurer leadership; the site lists insurers with their CEOs. 
 Gaps & open questions No published enforcement or code-discipline record — the council's consumer relevance depends on machinery that is not publicly traceable. Grievance data is not published by the council; consumer complaints flow to insurers and IRDAI's Bima Bharosa instead. 
 Sources List of member insurers — Life Insurance Council Life Insurance Council website 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from LI Council’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry

## GI Council work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-gic.html
What GI Council actually does 
 General Insurance Council GI Council 
 Statutory self-regulatory council for general and health insurance (Insurance Act s.64C, IRDAI) 

 The General Insurance Council (GIC) is the statutory self-regulatory body for the general, health and reinsurance industry under section 64C of the Insurance Act, 1938. Its 49 members (badge count on the council's own member page) include standalone health insurers, public-sector insurers, and reinsurance operations in India (GIC Re, Swiss Re, Lloyd's, AXA France VIE and General Re branches). 
 Statutory role Self-regulation of the non-life industry: promoting efficiency, fair practices and public interest; advising government and IRDAI. Publishes a Code of Good Insurance Practices; runs industry working groups on claims, health and co-insurance (ETASS). Anchor of IRDAI's 'Insurance for All by 2047' industry-side work. Membership (captured 2026-09-26) 49 members captured from gicouncil.in's member grid (the page advertises '49 Members'). Composition includes general insurers, standalone health insurers (Care, Niva Bupa, ManipalCigna, Galaxy, Prudential HCL) and reinsurance branches. 
 Gaps & open questions The member page is a JS-rendered grid (Angular) — roster requires a browser capture, which weakens reproducibility. No published discipline/enforcement log; practice codes lack a dated compliance trail. 
 Sources Member companies — General Insurance Council General Insurance Council website 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from GI Council’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry

## IIIPI work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-iiipi.html
What IIIPI actually does 
 Indian Institute of Insolvency Professionals of ICAI IIIPI 
 First registered insolvency professional agency — ICAI (IBBI/IPA/16-17/01) 

 The Indian Institute of Insolvency Professionals of ICAI (IIIPI) is a section-8 company wholly owned by ICAI, registered with IBBI as an Insolvency Professional Agency (registration IBBI/IPA/16-17/01 — first of the three agencies) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. IPAs enrol insolvency professionals as members and enforce the code of conduct on them. 
 Mandate & machinery Enrol insolvency professionals (IPs) as professional members; lay down standards; monitor and discipline members under the IBBI (Insolvency Professionals) Regulations 2016. Governed by a board with independent directors; operates disciplinary committees for member conduct. Registers IP rosters live in IBBI's own registers (individual IP registration numbers begin IBBI/IPA-001/... for IIIPI members); IIIPI does not publish a simple member directory. 
 Gaps & open questions Member counts and disciplinary outcomes are scattered across IBBI board reports and individual orders — no single public enforcement ledger. 
 Sources Registered Insolvency Professional Agencies — IBBI IIIPI (ICAI) website 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from IIIPI’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry

## ICSI IIP work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-icsiip.html
What ICSI IIP actually does 
 ICSI Institute of Insolvency Professionals ICSI IIP 
 Insolvency professional agency of ICSI (IBBI/IPA/16-17/02) 

 ICSI Institute of Insolvency Professionals (ICSI IIP) is a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (section 8), registered with IBBI as the second Insolvency Professional Agency (IBBI/IPA/16-17/02). It enrols company-secretary-route insolvency professionals and enforces the IBBI code of conduct. 
 Mandate & machinery Enrolment, monitoring and discipline of IPs; standards development; continuing education for insolvency practice. Its own site describes it as a 'frontline regulator registered with IBBI under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016'. Registers Member IP registration numbers carry the IBBI/IPA-002/ prefix; the authoritative register is IBBI's. 
 Gaps & open questions No aggregated public record of complaints and disciplinary orders against its members.

## AMFI work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-amfi.html
What AMFI actually does 
 Association of Mutual Funds in India AMFI 
 Mutual funds' association — self-regulatory in practice, not by recognition (SEBI context entry) 

 The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI, est. 1995, CIN U65991MH1995NPL092062) is the mutual-fund industry's association. It behaves self-regulatorily — codes of conduct for AMCs and distributors, the ARN registration regime — but SEBI has never granted it formal SRO recognition (a gap documented in the World Bank's 2007 SRO policy note, and unchanged by SEBI's 2024 SRO framework, which covers stock brokers, IAs and RAs). 
 Self-regulatory work AMFI Code of Conduct for AMCs; codes and norms for distributors (ARN holders) incl. investor-protection and conduct rules. Industry data office: daily/weekly/monthly MF folio and AUM statistics that underpin most sector reporting. Investor-awareness programmes (AMFI-appointed 'Mutual Funds Sahi Hai' campaign). Membership (captured 2026-09-26) 56 member AMCs listed on amfiindia.com's Members tab (from 360 ONE and Abakkus to Zerodha and old-line sponsors). Count has grown rapidly with new AMC licences (Angel One, Capitalmind, AlphaGrep, Groww, Helios et al). 
 Gaps & open questions Not a recognised SRO: no SEBI-granted disciplinary mandate; distributor discipline (ARN suspensions) exists but without a dated public trail. A 'context' register row — upgraded to tracked only if SEBI formalises an MF-sector SRO. 
 Sources AMFI Members — amfiindia.com (Members tab) World Bank SRO Policy Note (2007) 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from AMFI’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry


## ANMI register entry — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/sro-anmi.html

 Association of National Exchanges Members of India ANMI 
 Deep-dive: what ANMI actually does → 
 Stock brokers (NSE, BSE, MSE trading members) 

 Recognised (SEBI) — (association, 1996) 
 Status Industry body — not a recognised SRO 
 Listed members n/p (no public roster) 
 Site anmi.in 

 Why it matters if you borrow or pay 
 ~900 stock brokers' pan-India association — the voice arguing your broker's regulatory burden up or down — that has campaigned for formal SRO status without getting it. Its members hold the customer funds and margins SEBI keeps tightening rules on; ANMI self-regulates by code, not by recognition. Context entry: if SEBI ever recognises a brokers' SRO under its 2024-25 framework, ANMI is the likely candidate. 

 What we're watching 
 ANMI's own press releases say it 'seeks SRO status' — a public record of its non-recognition. Watch SEBI's brokers-SRO work for a recognition decision that would move ANMI into the tracked register.

## ANMI work deep-dive — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/work-anmi.html
What ANMI actually does 
 Association of National Exchanges Members of India ANMI 
 Stock brokers' pan-India association — campaigning for SRO status (SEBI context entry) 

 The Association of National Exchanges Members of India (ANMI, est. 1996) is a pan-India body of ~900 trading members of NSE, BSE and MSE. It engages SEBI and the exchanges on brokerage-industry issues but is not a recognised SRO; its own press releases solicit 'SRO status and a greater say in policy making'. 
 Profile & work Representation and advocacy: pre-budget memoranda, regulatory feedback, compliance seminars for brokers across exchanges. Runs an annual capital-market conference graced by the Finance Minister and SEBI Chairman; publishes a magazine. Board of directors drawn from member-broker leadership; committees for exchange-specific member segments. Membership ~900 active stock brokers (ASIFMA profile; ANMI's own 'about' describes a pan-India body of trading members of NSE/BSE/MSE). No public member directory; membership rosters sit behind the member area login. 
 Gaps & open questions Not a recognised SRO — included as context because it is the most probable candidate if SEBI recognises a brokers' SRO under the 2024-25 framework work. Self-description ('Voice of Capital Market') is marketing, not regulatory standing. 
 Sources ANMI website ANMI profile — ASIFMA 
 Captured 2026-09-10–11 from ANMI’s own site. Deep-dive under methodology · ← register entry


## Blog post: 2026-09-11-srotrac-weekly-1 — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/blog/2026-09-11-srotrac-weekly-1.html
---
title: "SROTrac Weekly #1 — UFF's licence, FEDAI's transition, and a tracker goes live"
date: 2026-09-11
summary: "The week India got its second fintech SRO; what the full RBI SRO map looks like; why rosters matter and who won't publish theirs."
---

# SROTrac Weekly #1

_Week to 11 September 2026_

## The big event: UFF gets its SRO-FT licence

The Reserve Bank formally recognised the **Unified Fintech Forum (UFF)** — rebranded from the Digital Lenders Association of India in April 2025 — as the **second SRO for the fintech sector**, at the Global Fintech Fest on 10 September. UFF joins **FACE** (recognised August 2024) under the SRO-FT framework. With this, both major fintech industry bodies are inside RBI's self-regulation perimeter: codes of conduct, member monitoring and grievance machinery that consumers can (in principle) invoke.

What makes UFF interesting on paper: its board carries heavyweight independent directors — former RBI Deputy Governor **N S Vishwanathan**, former RBI ED **Dr Meena Hemchandra**, ex-SIDBI CMD **Mohammad Mustafa**, and veteran banker **Alok Prasad** as Chair. Its executive committee has a dedicated **SRO portfolio** (chair: Progcap, co-chair: Vivifi). The test now is whether any of this machinery produces visible member discipline — FACE's enforcement record, for contrast, is unpublished.

## The full RBI SRO map, as of this week

| SRO | Sector | Recognised | Members published? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| MFIN | NBFC-MFIs | 16 Jun 2014 | Yes — ~84 listed |
| Sa-Dhan | NBFC-MFIs | Mar 2015 | No — via BMR report/portal |
| FACE | Fintech (SRO-FT) | 28 Aug 2024 | Yes — 85 listed |
| FIDC | NBFCs | 3 Oct 2025 | No — claims ~400 in press |
| SRPA | Payment system operators | 11 Nov 2025 | Yes — 18 logos |
| UFF | Fintech (SRO-FT) | 10 Sep 2026 | Yes — ~120 logos |
| FEDAI | Authorised dealers (FX) | 14 Jan 2026 | Yes — 108 with LEIs |

Seven RBI-recognised SROs, spanning microfinance (2014 origin), fintech, NBFCs, payments and now the forex market. Two patterns worth a consumer's attention:

1. **Publication asymmetry.** Six of eight publish full rosters (FACE, UFF, SRPA, MFIN, FEDAI and now Sahamati) with member websites. FIDC and Sa-Dhan — between them covering most of India's NBFC and MFI lending — publish none. A consumer cannot check whether their lender answers to an SRO unless the SRO says who its members are.
2. **Transition debt.** FEDAI has until January 2027 to align with the Omnibus SRO framework. SRPA's public face remains a one-page site with no code of conduct published. Recognition is the start of the accountability story, not the end.

## Why we built SROTrac

SROs sit between regulator and industry: they write the codes, monitor conduct, and are supposed to be the first door a complainant knocks on. But their public output — rosters, governance, consultation responses, enforcement actions — is scattered across six websites of varying quality. SROTrac consolidates the register, the member lists, the boards, and the activity trail in one place, with source snapshots for every claim. Everything here is re-verified daily by an automated refresh; roster changes are diffed and logged.

## Watchlist for next week

- UFF's first public act under the SRO-FT banner — a code of conduct? An enforcement note?
- Whether FIDC publishes a member roster or stays a ~400-member claim in press releases.
- FEDAI's membership expansion beyond AD Category-I banks (the one-year clock is running).

---

_SROTrac is an independent CashlessConsumer project. Data: [members](/members.html), [timeline](/timeline.html), [activity log](/activity.html). Corrections welcome._



## Blog post: 2026-09-14-srotrac-weekly-2 — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/blog/2026-09-14-srotrac-weekly-2.html
---
title: "SROTrac Weekly #2: Register completes at nine SROs; FIMMDA stands up discipline"
date: 2026-09-14
summary: "All nine RBI-recognised SROs now tracked on SROTrac. FIMMDA constituted its first disciplinary committee; GFF 2026 put regulatory gap-hopping on notice."
---

# SROTrac Weekly #2

_Week to 14 September 2026_

## TL;DR

- The register is now complete: SROTrac tracks **all nine RBI-recognised SROs**, with **642 members** across the seven rosters that are actually published. Additions this week: **FIMMDA** (financial markets) and **Sahamati** (account aggregators).
- FIMMDA constituted a **Disciplinary Committee of the Board** on 1 September — its first visible enforcement machinery since RBI recognition in May 2025.
- At Global Fintech Fest, RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra warned fintechs against "structuring business around gaps between regulatory categories, scaling first and seeking clarity later" — exactly the conduct SRO codes are supposed to catch first.

## Roster & register changes

Two additions took the register from seven SROs to the full set of nine.

**FIMMDA joins as SRO #9.** The Fixed Income Money Market and Derivatives Association of India was RBI's first SRO in the financial markets — recognised 7 May 2025 under the August 2024 framework for such SROs (Press Release 2025-2026/274). Its only public roster is a PDF dated 8 May 2025, listing **116 institutions**: 12 public sector banks, 21 private banks, 34 foreign banks, 7 primary dealers, 5 financial institutions, 20 insurers, 11 small finance banks, 3 payments banks, CCIL and 2 infrastructure financiers. One watch item we've flagged on its work page: FIMMDA's own site overview still claims to be "115 member strong" with category counts that don't match the PDF. We treat the PDF as the primary source and re-check on refresh.

**Sahamati joins as SRO #8.** Recognised 5 June 2026 as the SRO for the Account Aggregator ecosystem — the consent plumbing that lets you share bank statements with a lender or advisor without handing over credentials. Sahamati publishes a live register of **110 Account Aggregator and related regulated entities**, which we now track.

Elsewhere in the rosters: UFF holds steady at **121** members, and its homepage was updated on 12 September to lead with "RBI-recognized Self-Regulatory Organization" — recognition is now the first thing the site says about itself. FACE (85), MFIN (84), FEDAI (108) and SRPA (18) are unchanged this week. **FIDC and Sa-Dhan still publish no member roster at all** — two of nine SROs, and between them most of India's NBFC and microfinance lending, remain unverifiable by any consumer trying to check whether their lender answers to a code of conduct.

We also merged the members and overlap views into a single page with entity-type filters: 71 organisations sit in more than one SRO, and bank treasuries dominate the FIMMDA–FEDAI overlap.

## Regulatory & consultation watch

The week's policy backdrop was Global Fintech Fest (9–11 September, Mumbai). Governor Malhotra's keynote on 10 September announced UFF's recognition (covered last week) alongside UPI Tap & Pay, an AI-powered MyUPI, and a framework for corporate bond tokenisation — that last one lands squarely in FIMMDA's fixed-income domain, making it the one SRO with a direct stake in how tokenised bond market plumbing gets standardised.

The sharper line was aimed at regulatory arbitrage: Malhotra cautioned fintechs against a mindset of structuring business around gaps between regulatory categories — scale first, seek clarity later. He also corrected the record on RBI's AI work: the model risk management document is guidance, not regulation, with a fuller AI governance framework for the financial sector still to come.

FIMMDA, meanwhile, quietly built the thing most SROs don't show you: a **Disciplinary Committee of the Board**, constituted 1 September under Article 34 of its Articles (circular FIMCIR/2026-27/20), chaired by independent director Manoj Rane, with Abhijit Basak (Union Bank) and Manish Luharuka (ICICI Bank). It's the first post-recognition enforcement machinery visible on its site. Note the composition: two of three members are employed by member banks. Independence from dominant firms is precisely the test the SRO model sets for itself — the Governor's own GFF framing was that an SRO's credibility depends on broad membership, independence from dominant firms, transparent standards and meaningful action against non-compliance.

## What it means for consumers

- **Your bank's treasury desk now has a watchdog with a committee.** FIMMDA's members price your forex card rates, corporate borrowing benchmarks and money-market instruments. Retail consumers never see this SRO work directly — but its standards flow into every rate you're quoted. A disciplinary committee is the right machinery; the test is whether it ever publishes an outcome.
- **Consent data gets an SRO.** If you've shared financial data through an account aggregator, the ecosystem's 110 regulated entities now sit under Sahamati's code of conduct. That's a better escalation path than a lone complaint to a fintech app.
- **You still can't check most NBFC/MFI lenders.** FIDC and Sa-Dhan publish no rosters. Nine SROs tracked, but consumer-verifiable accountability still covers only the seven that publish.
- **The gap warning cuts both ways.** If a lender or payments app's business model depends on sitting between regulatory categories, its SRO membership is the first place standards should be enforced — before RBI has to act. Watch whether UFF's first code-of-conduct document names the gap-hopping practices the Governor described.

## Blog post: 2026-09-21-srotrac-weekly-3 — https://srotrac.cashlessconsumer.in/blog/2026-09-21-srotrac-weekly-3.html
---
title: "SROTrac Weekly #3: UPI gets a price tag; rosters hold steady"
date: 2026-09-21
summary: Rosters hold at 642 members, but UPI's zero-fee era ends Oct 15 — 0.4% MDR above ₹2,000 reshapes the economics of SRPA's payment-operator members.
---

# SROTrac Weekly #3

_Week to 21 September 2026_

## TL;DR

- A quiet week on the register: all nine tracked SROs unchanged, rosters steady at **642 members** across the seven lists actually published. This week's story sits in SRPA's backyard, not its register.
- UPI's zero-fee era for large merchant payments ends **15 October**: an MDR of up to **0.4% on P2M transactions above ₹2,000**, capped at ₹300 for ₹75,000-plus. Consumers keep paying nothing.
- The microfinance SROs made the week's second story: Sa-Dhan sought an extension of the ₹20,000-crore MFI credit guarantee scheme — barely ₹8,000–9,000 crore used — while MFIN's data shows portfolio quality recovering sharply.

## Roster & register changes

None — and we verified rather than assumed. The daily refresh ran all week (source re-fetch + rebuild), and a git diff of every member CSV since Weekly #2 shows zero changes. FACE holds at 85 members, UFF at 121, FIMMDA at 116, FEDAI at 108, Sahamati at 110, MFIN at 84, SRPA at 18. FIDC and Sa-Dhan still publish no roster at all — two of nine SROs, and between them most of India's NBFC and microfinance lending, remain unverifiable by any consumer who wants to check whether their lender answers to a code of conduct. That is now the register's oldest open item.

Post-recognition, UFF's homepage continues to lead with "RBI-recognized Self-Regulatory Organization". No new circulars or member announcements from it this week — recognition weeks are quieter than recognition days.

## Regulatory & consultation watch

**The week belonged to UPI's price tag.** The Finance Ministry's notification (Gazette, 14 September) locks in zero charges on UPI payments up to ₹2,000 and free person-to-person transfers. The next day NPCI circularised the other side: an MDR of up to 0.4% on specified person-to-merchant transactions above ₹2,000, effective 15 October 2026, confirmed in a joint DFS–NPCI FAQ and Paytm's exchange filing. The carve-outs matter as much as the headline rate: specified sectors — railways, telecom, insurance, fuel, farm inputs, together roughly 46% of P2M value — pay a flat ₹5 per transaction above ₹2,000; capital-market payments (mutual funds, securities) pay 0.02% capped at ₹300; transactions of ₹75,000 and above are capped at ₹300; and small merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh a month through UPI QR (the P2PM category) stay at zero MDR. NPCI says over 95% of merchant payment volume is ₹2,000 or less; brokerages put the above-threshold slice at about 4% of volume but around two-thirds of value.

**Where is the SRO in this?** SRPA — the SRO for payment system operators, 18 members — exists so this industry has standards machinery when the money rules change. But the MDR framework was set by the government and NPCI, not by any SRO. The live question for SRPA's constituency is now distribution: payment aggregators pushed for a fixed, direct share of the MDR pool, and ran into the structural fact that PAs are not direct NPCI members (Business Standard, 27 August — pre-week, still unresolved). We found no public SRPA statement on the framework as of writing; that is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence. The RBI's position: MDR is "a charge within the merchant payment ecosystem", not on customers, and fair distribution across participants supports investment in acceptance networks.

**Microfinance's SROs asked for time on the guarantee ladder.** Sa-Dhan confirmed it sought an extension of CGSMFI 2.0, the ₹20,000-crore credit guarantee scheme for MFIs: utilisation is likely only ₹8,000–9,000 crore, with larger MFIs sanctioned but not drawing down while smaller ones struggled to access it (Sa-Dhan CEO Jiji Mammen, ETBFSI, 20 September). The same report quotes MFIN data: PAR 31–180 days down to 1.6% at 30 June from 5.6% a year earlier, and funding to MFIN-member NBFC-MFIs up 91.4% year-on-year. A stress cycle cooling off — with both SROs arguing the guarantee shouldn't lapse while smaller lenders are still climbing back.

## What it means for consumers

- **You still pay nothing on UPI.** All P2P and all user-side UPI stays free; the 0.4% is a merchant-side fee on the ~4% of transactions above ₹2,000, with caps and flat-₹5 sectors. If an app or shop tells you UPI "now costs 0.4%", that's not the rule — it may be pass-through.
- **Watch the small print on 15 October.** Small merchants under ₹1 lakh/month on UPI QR keep zero MDR, but retailers expect some pass-through or a cash rethink, and enforcement is the hard part — multiple QR IDs can blur who counts as small. Your test is simple: does the price you're charged change beyond what the seller chooses?
- **Microfinance borrowers got good news in the data** — delinquencies down, funding up. Sa-Dhan's ask is that credit guarantees keep covering smaller MFIs; if the scheme lapses, it would show up in smaller-lender funding costs, and eventually in your loan pricing.
- **FIDC and Sa-Dhan still don't publish rosters.** The cheapest thing an SRO can offer a consumer is a list of who signed its code. Two of nine haven't. After a week in which payment-economics decisions came from government and NPCI, remember why SRO accountability matters: these bodies ask for the power of self-regulation — the public should be able to see who they regulate.
